trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
The line must go up: left is number 6, which comes later; right is number 4, which comes later.
Going left would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes right.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.

Going up would leave both cell (1,4) and number 10 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would force the line onto number 10 before its turn (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down.
Going right would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Going down would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Cell (6,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going up would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2). So the line goes right.
The line must go up: right is number 11, which comes later.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes through the portal to (5,5).
Cell (6,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
